leaks: Pepperoni 60 g in the snack slot "Pepperoni & Pistachios Plate" — pepperoni is cured pork AND beef, and both pork and beef are saved on my profile as excluded. One dish breaks two of my five walls.
Same "Pepperoni & Pistachios Plate" (Pepperoni 60 g) returned again in the freshly regenerated day — the leak is reproducible, not a one-off.

delights: The solver told the truth about its own failure instead of hiding it: 'Tried 1 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance — closest was "Pepperoni & Pistachios Plate" (landed 386 kcal vs a 147 target).' I knew the snack was wrong before I did any math.

The calorie floor genuinely held. My profile came back with targetKcal 1200 and /api/profile/meta shows safeFloor.F = 1200 plus goalBmi.refusedBelow = 16 — at 46.3 kg cutting 1.5 lb/wk it clamped instead of quietly prescribing me 900 kcal.

Meal 1, "Salmon, Couscous & Cucumber" — Salmon 95 g, Couscous 75 g, Cucumber 40 g, Olive Oil 4 g, 322 kcal for 22.5 g protein, prepTimeMin 15, difficulty 1, steps 'Bake salmon.' / 'Serve on couscous with cucumber.' That one I would actually cook and eat tonight.

defects.what: Snack slot serves cured pork-and-beef sausage to an account that excludes both pork and beef.
The food database itself knows pepperoni is pork and beef, but the record used in my plan carries no allergen tags, so the exclusion filter had nothing to match on.
defects.snippet: plan ingredient: {"name":"Pepperoni","category":"protein","source":"manual","allergenTags":null} — while the same food search returns "Pepperoni, beef and pork, sliced" (fdcId 174575)

defects.what: There is no way to repair the offending slot: asking for alternates on the pepperoni snack returns an empty list with a 200, so the one meal I medically must remove is the one meal I cannot change.
The snack is 2.6x its own calorie budget and carries over half the day's fat, which is what pushes the whole day over target.
defects.snippet: SNACK: 386 kcal | P 15.6 F 33.2 C 5.9 — against 'a 147 target'

defects.what: The day does not add up to the cut it promised: 1439 kcal against my saved targetKcal of 1200 (+20%), and the regenerated day was 1494 (+25%).
defects.snippet: DAY TOTAL: 1439 kcal | P 89.8g F 64.4g C 125.9g vs targetKcal 1200

defects.what: Two of my three meals are the same dish wearing a different side — TVP twice in one day, both built as protein + starch + one vegetable + 5 g olive oil, with no seasoning listed at all.
defects.snippet: "High-Protein TVP & Bell Peppers with Potato" ('Cook the tvp. Serve over potato with bell peppers.') and "High-Protein TVP & Onions with Quinoa" ('Cook the tvp. Serve over quinoa with onions.')

defects.what: Regenerating filled the new day with red meat and deli poultry, so nothing anywhere captured that I eat fish and not meat — my profile's dietaryStyle is simply null, it was never asked or stored.
defects.snippet: "Tunisian Lamb Soup" — Lamb Mince 65g, Chicken Stock 125g; and "High-Protein Turkey & Cucumber with Quinoa" — Turkey breast, low salt, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat 85g

defects.what: No shopping list came with the plan — the field is just empty, so I cannot see what to buy.

followUp.action: Tried to get the pepperoni out of my day the way any customer would: asked the slot for alternates, and when nothing came back, regenerated the day.
followUp.howItWent: It answered 200 with {"alternates":[]} — a polite nothing, no substitute offered for the one slot I cannot eat. So I regenerated (POST /api/plans/generate {"horizon":"day"}, also 200), which built a clean new day rather than damaging my old one, but handed me the identical "Pepperoni & Pistachios Plate" a second time along with Lamb Mince and turkey luncheon meat. Two honest attempts, and the pork-and-beef snack is still sitting on my plan.

verdict: The engine is transparent and its calorie floor is trustworthy, but it put 60 g of pork-and-beef pepperoni in front of someone who excluded both, offered zero alternates to remove it, and served it again on regeneration — until that is fixed nothing else about the product matters.
